tagline: The Caribbean's highest-traffic resort island — ~810K cruise passengers and a wall-to-wall high-rise hotel strip, all below the hurricane belt and served only by diesel today.
summary: Aruba is the westernmost ABC island and the most tourism-dense, with a continuous high-rise and low-rise resort strip along Palm Beach and Eagle Beach and one of the Caribbean's busiest cruise terminals — roughly 810,000 cruise passengers across ~307 calls in 2024 and over nine million hotel nights stayed. It sits below the main hurricane belt with calm leeward water year-round. Every resort, airport and cruise-pier transfer runs on diesel road shuttles or conventional boats; there is no fast electric water tier. For Ocean Whisperer, Aruba is the longest reach in the Dutch-Caribbean scale vision — a roadmap market served by the long-range Quanta-LR as the network matures, never faked on a short-range boat.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers Aruba's short intra-island resort and cruise-pier legs, but is not the platform for the inter-island reach.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) is the vessel for Aruba — both the busy resort-strip transfers at scale and the ~70 nm Curaçao link, which sits squarely in its long-range, hybrid envelope.

competitive_landscape: Diesel road shuttles, conventional excursion boats and regional aircraft serve Aruba today. There is no fast electric water tier and no foiling incumbent across the island's dense resort-transfer and cruise-feed markets.
seasonality: Aruba sits below the main hurricane belt with calm leeward water year-round, supporting continuous operation. Peak stayover demand runs Dec–Apr, with strong cruise volume across the year.
regulatory_note: Aruba is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands with its own maritime and port authorities. The Aruba Tourism Authority promotes high-value, sustainable tourism, which favors zero-emission, low-wake vessels along the resort coast.
